9 Common Mistakes in Punjab Govt Exam Preparation

2 min readBeginnerPunjab Police Sub Inspectorpreparation mistakesexam strategypsssbpunjab police
Quick answer

Skipping previous papers, daily current affairs on YouTube, cutting sleep, mocks in an AC room: 9 mistakes that cost aspirants marks, and the fix for each.

HA
Written & reviewed by Gurpreet Singh Published 18 November 2026
ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ
Share 🔗 Copy link WhatsApp Telegram X

These are the mistakes I have seen many students make, and one of them I made myself. With each mistake is what to do instead.

#MistakeDo this instead
1Skipping previous year papersSolve PYQs in the last 3 months. I made this mistake myself: 613 marks, cut-off 623.
2Daily current affairs from YouTube and websitesMonthly magazine, finished in one day, then revised 4-5 times
3Sitting with a book open but not studyingWhatever you study, study it with discipline and properly
410 hours in week one, quitting in week threeStart with 2-3 shifts and add slowly; studying every day matters most
5Cutting sleep to study moreSleep 8 hours daily; take study hours from the day's shifts
6Sitting down to study after parathas or a full mealEat light food that does not make you sluggish
7Studying but never revisingThe 1-7-30 rule: next day, after a week, after 30 days
8Too few mock tests, or taking them in an AC roomAt least 100 mocks, in exam conditions
9Taking negative people's words to heartMeet them less; answer with your result

Each fix is explained in detail in my separate blogs. All the links are on my Punjab Police SI Preparation Strategy page.

Straight answers

Frequently asked questions

What is the biggest mistake in government exam preparation?

Skipping previous year papers. I made this mistake myself in my first SI attempt: 613 marks against a cut-off of 623.

Is it a mistake to read current affairs daily on YouTube?

For most aspirants, yes. Daily videos scatter your notes and eat time. One monthly magazine finished in a day and revised 4-5 times works better.
